title: Regional Flow Shepherd: Coordinated active-active edge failover, stream affinity & load-shedding playbook
creator: Sanjay Patel
description: Goal: Define and implement a coordinated active-active edge failover pattern that minimizes customer-visible disruptions for short-lived API calls and long-lived streaming sessions while preserving SLOs and predictable error-budget burns. This ticket captures design, implementation steps, telemetry, and the operational playbook for runbooks and rollout. Key constraints: maintain low p50/p95 latency for non-degraded traffic, bound p99 tail from cascading failovers, and provide graceful streaming degradation (partial transcript preservation / deterministic fallback).
technical_design: High-level approach: 1) Per-request scoring + routing policy: compute a region health score (latency, error-rate, queue-depth, token-balance) and choose primary region for each request using sticky affinity tokens with TTL. 2) Two-layer circuit breakers: local-region soft-circuit (per-node, fast detection) and global-region hard-circuit (aggregated, conservative) with separate thresholds and cooldown windows. 3) Streaming handshake extension: embed ephemeral affinity token + stream-session version; on region shift, perform a short-lived proxy relay for remaining TTL to avoid breaking open streams. 4) Graceful degrade: when streaming cannot be preserved, return structured partial-result with deterministic resume token and stable fallback to a lower-throughput but more available model variant. 5) Load-shedding policy: reactive (score driven) and proactive (traffic shaping windows) modes; prefer shedding by token-class (background/low-priority customers) before dropping production-critical requests. 6) KV/Prefix cache sync: ensure KV cache pre-warm on target region during planned shift, with progressive warming using traffic mirroring. 7) Telemetry tagging: every request annotated with route_decision, origin_region, chosen_region, affinity_token, circuit_state, shed_reason (if dropped).
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Simulate traffic in staging with synthetic high-latency/failure injections and verify scoring decisions. Phase 1: Canary active for 5% of production traffic for low-risk orgs; observe error budget burn and p99. Phase 2: Open rollout to 25% with automatic rollback triggers tied to error budget and p99 delta. Phase 3: Full rollout with documentation and Ops runbook. Rollback criteria: sustained region p99 increase > 2x baseline for 5m or error budget burn > 30% in 1h. During rollout enable 'preserve-streams' flag only for customers on Dedicated/Demo tiers until stable.
telemetry_and_alerting: Metrics: regional_p50/p95/p99_latency, regional_error_rate, region_queue_depth, affinity_stickiness_ratio, partial_resume_success_rate
SLOs: total API availability >= 99.95% global; regional degradations allowed if global availability preserved. Per-customer streaming availability objective: 99.9% for sticky sessions for 5m windows
Alerts: page on region_health_score < 40 for > 2m; page on failover_count spike > 50 in 10m; warn on shed_rate > 1% for production tier
Logging: structured events for routing_decision and circuit_transitions sent to central observability with sampling for full traces
acceptance_criteria: Routing decisions must be reproducible in staging with the same inputs (region load, token TTL, customer priority)
Local soft-circuits trip and recover within expected windows without causing global circuit cascade in injected-failure scenarios
Active canary must not increase global error budget burn by more than 10% during a 24h test
Streams that are promoted during a regional shift should either be preserved via short-lived relay (>= 90% success) or return deterministic resume tokens enabling resumed continuity
Load-shedding must prioritize non-critical token classes and provide a clear shed_reason for metrics and billing reconciliation
Playbook documented and Ops team validated on rollback/runbook steps; runbook drill executed once before full release
